Subject: Feature parity: streaming & tool calls — follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap: 
- Goal: validate parity vs your current hyperscaler endpoints for streaming responses and reliable function/tool calling for the chat flows powering your support assistant.
- High-level gaps you care about: stable streaming (low tail latency), deterministic structured outputs (JSON schema), and secure function/tool invocation with retries and observability.

What we heard / Redwood differentiators: 
- Streaming: continuous token streaming with configurable flush behavior + per-token cost breakdown in Console so you can model economics.
- Tool/function calling: explicit schema enforcement, deterministic response selection, and built-in auth hooks for third-party tools.
- Observability: per-request tracing + token-level latency/cost and easy trace drilldowns to compare model variants.

Attachments: I attached a feature-parity matrix (redwood-feature-parity-matrix.xlsx) that maps your hyperscaler behaviors to Redwood's capabilities and a short test plan (acme-test-instructions.md).

Proposed next tests (we suggest running these in parallel over the next 7–10 business days): 
1) Streaming latency + tail behavior: 1k concurrent, avg customer message length 80 tokens, max session length 2,000 tokens. Measure p50/p95/p99 and continuous stream stalls. (Owner: Michael)
2) Tool calling deterministicity: invoke same tool payload 50x across model variants; assert schema validity and stable routing to the correct tool (Owner: Aditya).
3) Structured output validation: evaluate 500 prompts against your JSON schema; measure parse success and false-positive corrections. (Joint owners: Marissa + Alex)

Next steps / timeline: 
- Michael and Aditya to run benchmarks and share logs + runbook by EOD 2027-03-19.
- We’ll share a short eval contract/POA (DocuSign link below) so you can provision Dedicated eval capacity if needed.
- Follow-up sync Wed 2027-03-22 10:00am PT to review results — does that time still work for you?

Thanks — happy to adjust scope based on your priorities.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the matrix — useful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- For streaming tests, our biggest concern is the p99 tail under bursty load (we see spikes during high-traffic events). Can Michael include a run that simulates a traffic spike (10x baseline for 2–3 minutes)?
- For function calling: we use a multi-step orchestration where a single user turn can trigger up to 3 tool calls. We need to see that Redwood maintains call ordering and that retries don’t duplicate actions downstream.

Logistics/questions: 
- We can commit a small eval POA but procurement needs DocuSign and an SOW; would you be able to send the DocuSign link and a short SOW?
- Wed 3/22 10:00am PT works for Priya and me.

I’ll loop in our infra lead if you want deeper network test coordination (cc-ing Priya now).

Appreciate it,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
